question.text: Under PMLA Rules, when identifying the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) of an investor that is structured as a company investing in an AIF, what controlling-ownership-interest threshold applies?

answer.text: 25% controlling ownership interest for companies/trusts; 15% for partnership firms/unincorporated associations
5% controlling ownership interest for all investor types

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules: UBO identification uses 25% controlling ownership interest (or control) for company/trust investors and 15% ownership-or-entitlement for partnership firms and unincorporated associations of individuals. The AIF must identify the natural person(s) who ultimately own or control the investing institution. **The Trap:** Option A is the PFI threshold used for listed securities (not PMLA UBO). Option C/D are fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XXIV (AML) directly tests 25/15 split. XIX-C tests application to AIF onboarding. XXI-B (PM) also tests this. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: Maintain a UBO register alongside the Investor Register. For foreign investors, also screen UBO against UNSC Sanctions List and check FATF jurisdiction status. If UBO sits in a land-bordering country (per Rule 6 NDI Rules) and triggers the 50%/50% corpus/UBO threshold, the investee-company 10%-equity disclosure rule to custodian kicks in.
